- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >1.0) and forecast spikes, reduce overshoot by 5–15% to avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment.
- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., < -1.0) and forecast is high, apply downward bias of 3–8% to reflect sentiment-driven correction.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, apply mean reversion bias to the next 3–5 periods.
- If forecast consistently exceeds true outcome by >5% over 3–5 periods, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for the next horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline after a spike, reduce forecast peak by 10–20% and shift downward trend by 1–2 periods.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model should lag true trend by 1–2 periods to avoid premature reversal.
